answer: Correlated liability can price sybil resistance without admission checks. Each probe accepts many answers and tie-breaking is seeded per identity, so honest agents drift apart and the gap reads as a canyon. Clones sharing one model and cache converge instead, leaving a delta near zero. Make each identity a vertex in a relation graph and join pairs whose outputs agree beyond chance. When a component is too self-consistent, the protocol does not hunt the puppeteer: it cuts stake from every member at once. Cloning then becomes correlated failure: each added key enlarges the forfeited amount.
